public_rationale: The AI trade was still active on October 27. That does not show whether accelerating revenue and spending are necessary to sustain it. The search found no decisive, sustained counterexample meeting the early-resolution rule. With no deadline, the claim remains open.
limitations: The market report establishes only a short-term continuation of the trade.
The literal perpetual requirement cannot receive conclusive support from finite observations.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Keeping the AI trade going requires perpetual, parabolic growth in both AI revenues and AI capex.

statement.excerpt: The answer is simple: perpetual, parabolic growth in both AI revenues and AI capex.

from_speaker: both AI revenues and AI capex
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that sustained investor enthusiasm and elevated AI-related equity valuations require continuing, rapidly accelerating growth in both AI revenue and capital spending.
Parabolic is read colloquially, not as an exact quadratic function.
Keeping the party going refers to the broad AI investment trade, not every individual stock rising every day.
This is a necessary-condition claim. A continuing trade without the specified growth could disprove it; growth and rising stocks occurring together would not establish necessity.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence would need to establish that sustaining the AI trade depends on accelerating growth in both revenue and capital spending. Finite observations can support that mechanism but cannot establish the literal perpetual requirement.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable, realized revenue and capital-spending series show a sustained end to acceleration in either measure, while broad AI-related valuations remain sustained after investors have had time to absorb that information.
